channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: Duke maps the riches—and limits—of the 2026 public domain
item.description: Duke’s annual guide catalogs works from 1930 now free to use in the U.S., including early Betty Boop, Blondie, Nancy Drew and Sam Spade, plus films, songs and art. It also explains the archaeology behind the dates: only the original 1930 versions are newly public, while later adaptations and trademarks can still impose limits.
item.source: Duke Center for the Study of the Public Domain

item.title: Apache XMLBeans 5.4.1 ships with fixes and packaging cleanup
item.description: Apache has released XMLBeans 5.4.1, the Java library that binds XML schemas to generated Java types while also supporting DOM, cursors and schema reflection. The maintenance release brings bug fixes and packaging cleanup—a useful update for Java projects that still need rigorous, schema-aware XML processing.

item.title: Six new voices make the 4thWrite short-story shortlist
item.description: The 10th 4thWrite prize has shortlisted six unpublished writers of color whose stories range from office comedy and friendship to grief and dystopian London. The winner receives £1,000, a publishing workshop and publication in The Guardian, continuing a competition that has helped launch several writing careers.

item.title: WordPress documents three ways to import site content
item.description: A new WordPress developer guide compares three Blueprint import methods: WXR for portable posts and terms, PHP for deterministic fixtures, and ZIP snapshots for complete sites. It explains what each method moves, shows how WXR preserves content relationships and attachments, and includes benchmarks using a 100-post test site.

item.title: LitRPG turns self-published serials into publishing blockbusters
item.description: The rise of Dungeon Crawler Carl shows how a prolific online series can build a readership before traditional publishing arrives. Matt Dinniman’s first seven volumes were self-published online; the series has now sold 17 million copies and is headed for television. The piece explains how Royal Road became an incubator for game-shaped speculative fiction.

item.title: Lucas Museum puts popular narrative art in the gallery
item.description: The new Lucas Museum of Narrative Art treats comics, illustration, film design and other popular visual storytelling as museum-worthy art. Its 40,000-item founding collection ranges from manga and Frank Frazetta to Beatrix Potter, movie costumes and classic painting, with more than 1,200 works displayed across 30 galleries.

item.title: Garry Kitchen’s GameMaker lives again in a browser
item.description: GMC64 is a faithful browser recreation of Garry Kitchen’s 1985 Commodore 64 game-development system. The open-source project accepts original disk images and preserves its sprite, scene, sound and scripting workflow without requiring an emulator—a useful example of keeping a software-creation tool usable rather than merely archived.

item.title: What Ireland’s artists’ tax exemption does not cover
item.description: Ireland’s official guidance clarifies an important limit on its artists’ exemption: qualifying creative income may escape Income Tax, but not PRSI, VAT or the Universal Social Charge. The exemption also remains subject to the High Earners Restriction. It is a useful corrective to the shorthand claim that writers in Ireland simply pay no tax.

item.title: How Charlton’s Action Heroes became part of DC history
item.description: A compact guide traces the Charlton Action Heroes—including Ted Kord’s Blue Beetle, Captain Atom, the Question and Peacemaker—from their distinctive 1960s stories through DC’s acquisition and their indirect transformation into Watchmen. It is a useful map of why this small publisher’s characters continue to echo through modern comics and television.

item.title: WordPress developer roundup previews 7.2 and the latest Gutenberg changes
item.description: WordPress's September developer roundup covers changes in Gutenberg 23.8 and 23.9, practical tooling updates and the road to WordPress 7.2. Beta 1 is planned for late October and the final release for December, making this a useful early map of what plugin and theme developers should test.

item.title: Long-hidden Golden Age comic collection comes to auction
item.description: The newly surfaced Merrimack Valley Collection preserved major Golden Age comics for roughly 75 to 80 years. Its highlights include high-grade copies of Captain America Comics Nos. 1 and 3 and Batman's first nine issues—a rare original-owner time capsule from the formative superhero era.

item.title: ServiceNow folds its development environment into Studio
item.description: ServiceNow's September Creator update removes manual upgrades for its coding assistant and folds the ServiceNow IDE into Studio. The release also outlines features arriving with Brazil Early Availability, providing a concise look at how the platform's everyday development workflow is changing.

item.title: A forgotten box yields a Golden Age comics trove
item.description: The newly surfaced Merrimack Valley Collection spent 75 to 80 years in a cardboard box. Its exceptional Golden Age books include a 9.0 Captain America Comics No. 1, a 9.4 No. 3 containing Stan Lee's first Timely work, and Batman's first nine issues—eight graded 6.5 or higher.

item.title: Creative Commons meets Indigenous cultural authority
item.description: A new guide from Creative Commons and Local Contexts shows museums, archives and researchers how open licenses can work alongside Traditional Knowledge and Biocultural Labels. Case studies explain how the tools add provenance, community protocols and permissions that copyright alone cannot express.

item.title: St. Augustine dig finds its first British redoubt
item.description: A 15-foot-wide dry moat found in Lincolnville is the first physical evidence of one of seven British redoubts built around St. Augustine. The 1781 fortification survived only as marks on old maps until the city's archaeology program examined the lot before home construction and recovered thousands of plant remains.
